# chezmoi-dotfiles

This machine's `$HOME` is managed by a **chezmoi** (configs) + **ansible** (system
deps) dotfiles repo. This skill is the agent-facing map: how to drive it, and what
custom tooling exists that you wouldn't otherwise know about. It is rendered per-host
— the "What's enabled on THIS machine" section reflects what the user actually
selected at init.

## Orientation (read this first)

- **Repo root**: `chezmoi source-path` (no args) prints the source dir. Work there
  to edit: `cd "$(chezmoi source-path)"`.
- **Source path of one file**: `chezmoi source-path ~/.config/foo/bar` → the
  managed source file for that target.
- **`docs/**` is NOT deployed to `$HOME`** (it's chezmoi-ignored). Read detail via
  `"$(chezmoi source-path)/docs/..."`. A *subset* is deployed to `~/.config/docs/`
  (e.g. keybindings, cli-tools) for runtime helpers.
- **Read the contract before editing**: `"$(chezmoi source-path)/CLAUDE.md"` holds
  Hard invariants and cross-file maintenance rules. Honor them.
- This host: profile `macos_intel`, OS `darwin`/`amd64`, primary shell `zsh`.

## chezmoi essentials

```bash
chezmoi diff                 # preview changes (also: just chezmoi-diff)
chezmoi apply                # deploy + run scripts (also: cas, or just chezmoi-apply)
chezmoi status               # modified/added/removed targets
chezmoi edit ~/.zshrc        # edit the SOURCE of a target
chezmoi add  ~/.config/x     # start managing an existing file
chezmoi re-add               # pull live edits back into source
chezmoi managed | grep foo   # is X managed?
chezmoi cat ~/.config/x      # render a target without applying
chezmoi data | jq            # the template data (ground truth for the toggles below)
```

- **`cas`** = `chezmoi apply` + reload hint; **`cau`** = update from remote then apply
  (defined in `dot_config/shell/99_chezmoi_reload.sh`).
- **`dotcfg`** = reconfigure the init prompts on an already-set-up machine
  (`dotcfg` for the TUI, `dotcfg --set installLlmTools=true --yes` for one toggle,
  `dotcfg --dry-run` to preview). Shell twin: `czcfg`.
- **Never `chezmoi add` a `modify_`/`create_` target** — it overwrites the script.
- Full command cheat-sheet: `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`. Install-vs-upgrade is
  split: `chezmoi apply`/ansible is **install-only**; upgrades go through
  `just upgrade-*`.

## What's enabled on THIS machine

(Rendered from this host's selections. For live truth: `chezmoi data | jq`.)
- **Coding agents** — Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor, Codex, Gemini, Copilot (configs + CLIs). See `docs/tools/agent-overlays.md`, `docs/tools/agent-skills.md`.
- **Python uv tools** — mlflow, marimo, jupyter, etc. (powers the `mlf` CLI). See `docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md`.
- **Extra runtimes** — rust, bun, ruby via mise (+ cargo/gem tools). Node is always present.
- **LLM tools** — Ollama / LiteLLM / local models.
- **JS CLI tools** — standalone npm CLIs (e.g. readability-cli).
- **.NET tools** — .NET SDK (mise) + dotnet global tools.
- **IaC** — Azure CLI, Terraform, OpenTofu.
- **Media** — ffmpeg, ImageMagick, exiftool, libvips.
- **Media control** — nowplaying-cli + switchaudio-osx (macOS) / playerctl (Linux); unlocks full `sysplay`/`sysnow` (built-in `sysvol`/`sysmute` work regardless).
- **Networking** — nmap, mtr, httpie, gping, trippy.
- **Tunnels** — ngrok, cloudflared.
- **Vim mode** — shell modal editing + tmux vim nav (NOT Neovim/editors — those are always vim).

## Custom in-house CLIs (always deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin`, on PATH)

Each works from any cwd. Run with `--help`, or read `docs/tools/<name>.md`. Full list: `ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_dotfiles/bin/"`.

- **`fleet`** — cross-host ops over your machines: `fleet chezmoi apply`, `fleet hosts`, `fleet tmux`, `fleet info`, `fleet pueue`, `fleet exec`. See `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-exec.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md`.
- **`mlf`** — MLflow umbrella CLI + TUI dashboard (needs Python uv tools). Picker twin: `tv mlflow`.
- **`pqsum`** — pueue queue summary (text / AI / JSON). See `docs/tools/pueue.md`.
- **`x`** — clipboard/file copy-paste-open with cross-platform fallbacks.
- **`mi-router`** / **`reyee`** / **`sms`** — read-only router CLIs (Xiaomi MiWiFi / Ruijie Reyee / Huawei HiLink SMS). See `docs/tools/{mi-router,reyee,sms}.md`.
- **`ping-monitor`** — record ping over time, flag latency spikes. See `docs/tools/ping-monitor.md`.
- **`dotcfg`** — reconfigure dotfiles prompts (above).
- **`sesh-preview`** — preview helper for the sesh picker.

## Television (`tv`) — fuzzy pickers with custom channels

There are ~40 **custom** channels (system state, fleet, services, infra, agents…)
that you won't discover otherwise. Browse them:

```bash
tv                      # default picker
tv list-channels        # list everything available
tv <channel>            # open one, e.g. tv fleet-hosts | tv mlflow | tv pueue
ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_config/television/cable/"   # the channel definitions
```

Handy ones: `fleet-hosts`, `mlflow`, `pueue`, `ports`, `kill-process`, `services`,
`sessions`, `keybindings`, `aliases`, `git-ops`, `mac-apps`/`linux-apps`. Full
reference: `docs/tools/tv.md`.

## Keybindings & keymaps

- **`bindings`** (shell function) or **`tv keybindings`** — interactive reference.
- **tmux**: `prefix + Space` (or `prefix + e`) opens the action menu;
  `prefix + T` = sesh picker, `prefix + U` = tools. Deep ref: `docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md`.
- **shell ZLE widgets**: `Alt+S` sesh sessions, `Alt+T` tools, `Ctrl+R` history (atuin).
- Master reference: `docs/shells/keybindings.md` (also deployed to `~/.config/docs/shells/keybindings.md`).

## Aliases & functions

`alias` to list shell aliases, or `tv aliases`. Catalog: `docs/shells/aliases.md`.
Helpers worth knowing: `chezmoi-cd` (jump to source), `run-for` (time-box a command),
`bindings` (above). App control: `applaunch`/`appquit`/`apprestart`/… (cross-platform).
System audio (cross-platform, built-in): `sysvol`/`sysmute` (+ `sysplay`/`sysnow` with `installMediaControl`); remote mute via `fleet exec --login -- sysmute on`.

## just recipes (run from the source dir)

```bash
cd "$(chezmoi source-path)" && just --list
```

Categories: `chezmoi-*`, `ansible-*`, `upgrade-*` (brew/mise/uv/npm/cargo/…),
`fleet`/`fleet-*`, `gen-prompts` (regenerate prompt scaffolding), `check`/`lint`,
`docker-*`. See `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`.

## Editing rules (don't skip)

Before changing anything under the repo, read `CLAUDE.md` Hard invariants and the
"Cross-file maintenance rules" table — many surfaces have mandatory mirror updates
in the same commit (docs, completions, tool-managers index, this very skill, …).

```text
1	# 99_chezmoi_reload.sh - post-`chezmoi apply` reload hint + cas/cau wrappers
2	#
3	# Pattern:
4	#   - .chezmoiscripts/global/run_after_99_signal_reload.sh.tmpl touches the
5	#     sentinel ~/.cache/chezmoi/last-apply after every chezmoi apply.
6	#   - At shell init (here) we record this shell session's birth time as a
7	#     temp marker file.
8	#   - On every prompt a precmd / PROMPT_COMMAND hook calls _chezmoi_reload_check.
9	#   - Check fires AT MOST ONCE per shell session, then short-circuits.
10	#
11	# This file is the single source of truth. The shell-specific hook registration
12	# (add-zsh-hook for zsh, blehook/PROMPT_COMMAND for bash) lives at the bottom,
13	# dispatched by $ZSH_VERSION/$BASH_VERSION at source time. We do NOT use
14	# dot_config/{zsh,bash}/*99_chezmoi_reload.{zsh,bash} because the bash side
15	# would run before this file (dot_bashrc.tmpl loads $BASH_CONFIG_DIR before
16	# $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/shell to satisfy oh-my-bash's plugins=() prereq) and the
17	# backend function would not yet be defined.
18	#
19	# Opt out:
20	#   export CHEZMOI_RELOAD_HINT=0    # in ~/.shellrc.adhoc or a per-shell secret file
21	#
22	# Cross-file maintenance: see CLAUDE.md "Cross-file maintenance rules" row.
23	
24	[[ "${CHEZMOI_RELOAD_HINT:-1}" = "0" ]] && return 0
25	
26	_CZ_RELOAD_SENTINEL="${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/chezmoi/last-apply"
27	_CZ_RELOAD_BIRTH="$(command mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/.cz_birth.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)" || _CZ_RELOAD_BIRTH=""
28	
29	_chezmoi_reload_cleanup() {
30	    [[ -n "$_CZ_RELOAD_BIRTH" && -f "$_CZ_RELOAD_BIRTH" ]] && rm -f "$_CZ_RELOAD_BIRTH"
31	}
32	trap _chezmoi_reload_cleanup EXIT
33	
34	# Resolve the *current* shell interpreter rather than $SHELL (which reflects
35	# /etc/passwd / chsh and can lag the real interpreter on first login).
36	_chezmoi_reload_current_shell() {
37	    if [[ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]]; then
38	        printf 'zsh'
39	    elif [[ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ]]; then
40	        printf 'bash'
41	    else
42	        printf '%s' "$(basename "${SHELL:-sh}")"
43	    fi
44	}
45	
46	# Fires once per session. Hot-path returns when _CZ_RELOAD_SHOWN is set.
47	_chezmoi_reload_check() {
48	    [[ -n "$_CZ_RELOAD_SHOWN" ]] && return 0
49	    [[ -f "$_CZ_RELOAD_SENTINEL" ]] || return 0
50	    [[ -n "$_CZ_RELOAD_BIRTH" && -f "$_CZ_RELOAD_BIRTH" ]] || return 0
51	    [[ "$_CZ_RELOAD_SENTINEL" -nt "$_CZ_RELOAD_BIRTH" ]] || return 0
52	
53	    _CZ_RELOAD_SHOWN=1
54	    local sh rc
55	    sh="$(_chezmoi_reload_current_shell)"
56	    rc="~/.${sh}rc"
57	
58	    if [[ -t 1 ]] && command -v tput >/dev/null 2>&1; then
59	        local y c r
60	        y="$(tput setaf 3 2>/dev/null)"
61	        c="$(tput setaf 6 2>/dev/null)"
62	        r="$(tput sgr0 2>/dev/null)"
63	        printf '%sℹ%s chezmoi applied changes — run %sexec %s -l%s or %ssource %s%s to reload\n' \
64	            "$y" "$r" "$c" "$sh" "$r" "$c" "$rc" "$r"
65	    else
66	        printf 'i chezmoi applied changes - run `exec %s -l` or `source %s` to reload\n' \
67	            "$sh" "$rc"
68	    fi
69	}
70	
71	# Proactive wrappers: run instead of `chezmoi apply` / `chezmoi update` when
72	# you want the new shell rc to take effect immediately. exec's a fresh login
73	# shell on success so PATH, completions, hooks, prompts all reinitialise.
74	cas() {
75	    chezmoi apply "$@" || return $?
76	    local sh
77	    sh="$(_chezmoi_reload_current_shell)"
78	    exec "$sh" -l
79	}
80	cau() {
81	    chezmoi update "$@" || return $?
82	    local sh
83	    sh="$(_chezmoi_reload_current_shell)"
84	    exec "$sh" -l
85	}
86	
87	# czcfg - reconfigure dotfiles prompts on an already-initialized machine.
88	# Seeds the grouped TUI from your current chezmoi.toml values, then runs
89	# `chezmoi init --apply --prompt` (the SSOT wrapper, scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py)
90	# so changed answers actually take effect. `scripts/` isn't deployed, so we
91	# locate it via `chezmoi source-path`. Non-interactive single-key changes:
92	#   czcfg --set installLlmTools=true motdStyle=figlet --yes
93	# Does NOT exec a fresh shell itself — chezmoi apply's reload hint (above) does.
94	czcfg() {
95	    if ! command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
96	        printf 'czcfg: uv not found; install it first (https://astral.sh/uv).\n' >&2
97	        return 1
98	    fi
99	    local src
100	    src="$(chezmoi source-path 2>/dev/null)" || {
101	        printf 'czcfg: could not resolve chezmoi source-path.\n' >&2
102	        return 1
103	    }
104	    uv run --script "${src}/scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py" reconfigure "$@"
105	}
106	
107	# Hook registration — source-time dispatch by current shell. The other branch
108	# is never parsed at runtime, so zsh-only / bash-only syntax inside each
109	# branch is fine (but we keep both branches POSIX-clean anyway).
110	if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
111	    autoload -Uz add-zsh-hook 2>/dev/null
112	    add-zsh-hook precmd _chezmoi_reload_check
113	elif [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
114	    if [ -n "${BLE_VERSION:-}" ] && declare -f blehook >/dev/null 2>&1; then
115	        blehook PRECMD+=_chezmoi_reload_check
116	    else
117	        # Append without duplicating on re-source.
118	        case "${PROMPT_COMMAND:-}" in
119	            *_chezmoi_reload_check*) : ;;
120	            *) PROMPT_COMMAND="_chezmoi_reload_check${PROMPT_COMMAND:+;$PROMPT_COMMAND}" ;;
121	        esac
122	    fi
123	fi
124

12	# (add-zsh-hook for zsh, blehook/PROMPT_COMMAND for bash) lives at the bottom,
13	# dispatched by $ZSH_VERSION/$BASH_VERSION at source time. We do NOT use
14	# dot_config/{zsh,bash}/*99_chezmoi_reload.{zsh,bash} because the bash side
15	# would run before this file (dot_bashrc.tmpl loads $BASH_CONFIG_DIR before
16	# $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/shell to satisfy oh-my-bash's plugins=() prereq) and the
17	# backend function would not yet be defined.
18	#
19	# Opt out:
20	#   export CHEZMOI_RELOAD_HINT=0    # in ~/.shellrc.adhoc or a per-shell secret file
21	#
22	# Cross-file maintenance: see CLAUDE.md "Cross-file maintenance rules" row.
23	
24	[[ "${CHEZMOI_RELOAD_HINT:-1}" = "0" ]] && return 0
25	
26	_CZ_RELOAD_SENTINEL="${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/chezmoi/last-apply"
27	_CZ_RELOAD_BIRTH="$(command mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/.cz_birth.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)" || _CZ_RELOAD_BIRTH=""
28	
29	_chezmoi_reload_cleanup() {
30	    [[ -n "$_CZ_RELOAD_BIRTH" && -f "$_CZ_RELOAD_BIRTH" ]] && rm -f "$_CZ_RELOAD_BIRTH"
31	}
32	trap _chezmoi_reload_cleanup EXIT
33	
34	# Resolve the *current* shell interpreter rather than $SHELL (which reflects
35	# /etc/passwd / chsh and can lag the real interpreter on first login).
36	_chezmoi_reload_current_shell() {
37	    if [[ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]]; then
38	        printf 'zsh'
39	    elif [[ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ]]; then
40	        printf 'bash'
41	    else
42	        printf '%s' "$(basename "${SHELL:-sh}")"
43	    fi
44	}
45	
46	# Fires once per session. Hot-path returns when _CZ_RELOAD_SHOWN is set.
47	_chezmoi_reload_check() {
48	    [[ -n "$_CZ_RELOAD_SHOWN" ]] && return 0
49	    [[ -f "$_CZ_RELOAD_SENTINEL" ]] || return 0
50	    [[ -n "$_CZ_RELOAD_BIRTH" && -f "$_CZ_RELOAD_BIRTH" ]] || return 0
51	    [[ "$_CZ_RELOAD_SENTINEL" -nt "$_CZ_RELOAD_BIRTH" ]] || return 0
52	
53	    _CZ_RELOAD_SHOWN=1
54	    local sh rc
55	    sh="$(_chezmoi_reload_current_shell)"
56	    rc="~/.${sh}rc"
57	
58	    if [[ -t 1 ]] && command -v tput >/dev/null 2>&1; then
59	        local y c r
60	        y="$(tput setaf 3 2>/dev/null)"
61	        c="$(tput setaf 6 2>/dev/null)"
62	        r="$(tput sgr0 2>/dev/null)"
63	        printf '%sℹ%s chezmoi applied changes — run %sexec %s -l%s or %ssource %s%s to reload\n' \
64	            "$y" "$r" "$c" "$sh" "$r" "$c" "$rc" "$r"
65	    else
66	        printf 'i chezmoi applied changes - run `exec %s -l` or `source %s` to reload\n' \
67	            "$sh" "$rc"
68	    fi
69	}
70	
71	# Proactive wrappers: run instead of `chezmoi apply` / `chezmoi update` when
72	# you want the new shell rc to take effect immediately. exec's a fresh login
73	# shell on success so PATH, completions, hooks, prompts all reinitialise.
74	cas() {
75	    chezmoi apply "$@" || return $?
76	    local sh
77	    sh="$(_chezmoi_reload_current_shell)"
78	    exec "$sh" -l
79	}
80	cau() {
81	    chezmoi update "$@" || return $?
82	    local sh
83	    sh="$(_chezmoi_reload_current_shell)"
84	    exec "$sh" -l
85	}
86	
87	# czcfg - reconfigure dotfiles prompts on an already-initialized machine.
88	# Seeds the grouped TUI from your current chezmoi.toml values, then runs
89	# `chezmoi init --apply --prompt` (the SSOT wrapper, scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py)
90	# so changed answers actually take effect. `scripts/` isn't deployed, so we
91	# locate it via `chezmoi source-path`. Non-interactive single-key changes:
92	#   czcfg --set installLlmTools=true motdStyle=figlet --yes
93	# Does NOT exec a fresh shell itself — chezmoi apply's reload hint (above) does.
94	czcfg() {
95	    if ! command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
96	        printf 'czcfg: uv not found; install it first (https://astral.sh/uv).\n' >&2
97	        return 1
98	    fi
99	    local src
100	    src="$(chezmoi source-path 2>/dev/null)" || {
101	        printf 'czcfg: could not resolve chezmoi source-path.\n' >&2
102	        return 1
103	    }
104	    uv run --script "${src}/scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py" reconfigure "$@"
105	}
106	
107	# Hook registration — source-time dispatch by current shell. The other branch
108	# is never parsed at runtime, so zsh-only / bash-only syntax inside each
109	# branch is fine (but we keep both branches POSIX-clean anyway).
110	if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
111	    autoload -Uz add-zsh-hook 2>/dev/null
112	    add-zsh-hook precmd _chezmoi_reload_check
113	elif [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
114	    if [ -n "${BLE_VERSION:-}" ] && declare -f blehook >/dev/null 2>&1; then
115	        blehook PRECMD+=_chezmoi_reload_check
116	    else
117	        # Append without duplicating on re-source.
118	        case "${PROMPT_COMMAND:-}" in
119	            *_chezmoi_reload_check*) : ;;
120	            *) PROMPT_COMMAND="_chezmoi_reload_check${PROMPT_COMMAND:+;$PROMPT_COMMAND}" ;;
121	        esac
122	    fi
123	fi
124
```

 `./.chezmoiscripts/global/run_after_99_signal_reload.sh.tmpl`

```text
1	#!/bin/bash
2	# Touch a sentinel after every `chezmoi apply` so shells that were started
3	# before this apply can detect (on their next prompt) that dotfiles changed
4	# and remind the user to `source ~/.zshrc` or `exec $SHELL -l`.
5	#
6	# Wired up in:
7	#   - dot_config/shell/99_chezmoi_reload.sh    (shared backend, cas/cau, hook registration)
8	#
9	# Hook registration lives inside the shared backend (not per-shell tier dirs)
10	# because dot_bashrc.tmpl loads $BASH_CONFIG_DIR before $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/shell.
11	#
12	# `run_after_99_*` (not `run_onchange_after_*`) so it fires every apply --
13	# that's the signal we want. Cost is one `touch` per apply.
14	#
15	# Opt out (suppresses the hint in your shell sessions, sentinel still touched):
16	#   export CHEZMOI_RELOAD_HINT=0
17	
18	set -e
19	
20	cache_dir="${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/chezmoi"
21	mkdir -p "$cache_dir"
22	touch "$cache_dir/last-apply"
23
```
</details></tool-use>

1:# Custom Aliases & Shell Functions
3:Quick reference for custom aliases and shell functions defined in this dotfiles repo. Available in zsh, bash, or both — the source file path tells you which:
5:- `dot_config/shell/*.sh` — POSIX layer, sourced by **both** `~/.zshrc` and `~/.bashrc`.
9:> **Maintenance rule** (mirrored in `CLAUDE.md`): whenever you add, modify, or remove a custom alias or shell function in `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/`, update this table — include the type (`alias` or `function`), source file (relative to repo root), and a one-line description. Place new helpers in the right tier per the [CLAUDE.md three-tier rule](../../CLAUDE.md#custom-aliases--shell-functions--docsshellsaliasesmd).

Reuses `dot_config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh` helpers. |

2	#
3	# Init order (load-bearing — see docs/shells/bash.md):
4	#   1.  Early-return guard (non-interactive shells)
5	#   2.  /etc/bashrc source (RHEL families)
6	#   3.  ble.sh --attach=none   ← BEFORE bash-preexec / starship
7	#   4.  XDG dirs + Homebrew shellenv (mac)
8	#   5.  Bash-specific config files (history / completion / vi-mode / aliases)
9	#   6.  oh-my-bash source (after ble.sh so OMB's bash-preexec install no-ops)
10	#   7.  Shared modular layer (starship / mise / zoxide / direnv / thefuck)
11	#   8.  atuin init bash --disable-up-arrow (ble.sh handles up-arrow history)
12	#   9.  Secrets
13	#   10. ble-attach   ← absorbs all precmd/preexec stacks accumulated above
14	#   11. ~/.bash_aliases (Debian/Ubuntu) + ~/.bashrc.d/* (RHEL family)
15	#       — backward-compat with distro skel conventions
16	#   12. .bashrc.adhoc tail (chezmoi-ignored; highest-priority user override)
17	#
18	# The ble.sh / oh-my-bash / atuin steps are presence-gated and no-op
19	# silently when the artefact isn't installed (e.g. fresh host before
20	# `chezmoi apply` finishes the externals + run-onchange-after_install).
21	# Plain bash without ble.sh + OMB still gets a fully working starship
22	# prompt + the shared layer + bash-completion v2.
23	
24	# 1. ============================================================
25	# Non-interactive shells (SSH commands, cron, scp) bail out here.
26	# Anything below this guard runs only in interactive bash.
27	# Mirrors /etc/skel/.bashrc convention on Debian/Ubuntu.
28	case $- in
29	    *i*) ;;
30	      *) return ;;
31	esac
32	
33	# 2. ============================================================
34	# /etc/bashrc on RHEL families carries the protective `rm -i`
35	# aliases, the Modules system init, and umask defaults. Source it
36	# first so we don't lose those — and so anything we set below can
37	# override (we set HISTSIZE etc. larger than RHEL's defaults).
38	# Debian/Ubuntu has no /etc/bashrc, so this is a no-op there.
39	[ -r /etc/bashrc ] && . /etc/bashrc
40	
41	# 3. ============================================================
42	# ble.sh --attach=none lets us chain starship/atuin between this
43	# point and `ble-attach` at the end. Sourcing ble.sh AFTER
44	# bash-preexec (which starship installs) is the #1 ble.sh footgun
45	# documented at https://github.com/akinomyoga/ble.sh/wiki/
46	# So we source it FIRST, with --attach=none, then call ble-attach
47	# only at the very end. Presence-gated for hosts where
48	# .chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_NN_install_blesh.sh
49	# hasn't completed yet.
50	if [[ $- == *i* ]] && [ -r "$HOME/.local/share/blesh/ble.sh" ]; then
51	    # shellcheck disable=SC1091
52	    source "$HOME/.local/share/blesh/ble.sh" --attach=none --noattach
53	fi
54	
55	# 4. ============================================================
56	# XDG Base Directory Specification (mirrors dot_zshrc.tmpl)
57	export XDG_CONFIG_HOME="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}"
58	export XDG_DATA_HOME="${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}"
59	export XDG_CACHE_HOME="${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}"
60	
61	# Modular config directories
62	export BASH_CONFIG_DIR="$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/bash"
63	
64	{{ if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}
65	# Homebrew (macOS) — must run before shared layer so bash-completion v2's
66	# $HOMEBREW_PREFIX detection works.
67	if [[ -f /opt/homebrew/bin/brew ]]; then
68	    eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
69	elif [[ -f /usr/local/bin/brew ]]; then
70	    eval "$(/usr/local/bin/brew shellenv)"

76	# shares the same name + signature). Globs $dir/*.<ext> and sources

3	Cross-platform dotfiles managed by **chezmoi** (configs) + **ansible** (system deps). This file is the agent-facing contract: edit rules and cross-file invariants. User-facing intro: [README.md](README.md).

7	## Cross-file maintenance rules
8	
9	When you touch one of these surfaces, update the listed mirror in the same commit.
10	
11	| Surface you change | Also update | Reference |
12	|---|---|---|
13	| Config files / ansible roles / platforms / setup steps | `README.md` (What You Get, Supported Platforms, Quick Setup) | — |

43	### Workmux status icon integration spans 6 files
44	
45	Touching the `🤖`/`💬`/`✅` per-tmux-window status mechanism requires keeping these 6 surfaces in sync (full story: [docs/tools/workmux.md](docs/tools/workmux.md); pitfall: [pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md](pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md)):
46	
47	1. `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` — binary install (brew tap on macOS; GitHub release `.tar.gz` on Linux)
48	2. `dot_config/workmux/config.yaml` — `status_format: false` is load-bearing
49	3. `dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf` — `#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}` appended to `@catppuccin_window_text` and `@catppuccin_window_current_text`
50	4. `dot_claude/modify_settings.json` — `Stop`/`SubagentStop`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`Notification` hooks calling `workmux set-window-status` (hook-aware merger preserves CodeIsland entries)
51	5. `dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts` + `dot_config/opencode/modify_package.json`
52	6. `dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh` — generic POSIX `tmux_status_set/get/clear/clear_all/list/run` for non-agent producers
53	
54	**Hard rules**: never run `workmux setup` on a managed machine (would write parallel hook entries); never flip `status_format: true` (fights catppuccin's window-text override); never drop the `command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && … || true` guard in Claude hooks (spams errors on fresh boxes); never drop explicit `set-window-status done` from `Stop`/`SubagentStop` (upstream only ever sets `working`, never clears — that's the by-design leak documented in the pitfall). `wt` (worktrunk, `37_worktrunk.zsh`) and `wm` (workmux, `38_workmux.zsh`) stay distinct — different config formats, killer features, helper files.
55	
56	### Long-term backlog + past pitfalls → use the `project-knowledge-harness` skill
57	
58	This repo uses the `project-knowledge-harness` agent skill (restored on every `chezmoi apply` via `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl`; see [docs/tools/agent-skills.md](docs/tools/agent-skills.md)). **Load the skill** for the template, disambiguation table, and upgrade path.
59	
60	**Fallback rules** so this section still binds when the skill cannot be loaded:
61	
62	- Three repo-root surfaces, all chezmoi-ignored, all NOT auto-redacted: [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) (priority/effort tags `P1`/`P2`/`P3`/`P?` × `S`/`M`/`L`/`XL`), [`backlog/`](backlog/README.md) (research/design notes for `P?` / `[L]` / `[XL]` / multi-option), [`pitfalls/`](pitfalls/README.md) (debugged traps — **title by symptom, not root cause**, verbatim error messages, never paraphrase).
63	- Capture triggers — future work: "maybe later", "nice to have", "工程量太大需要再評估", "先記下來". Pitfalls: >~15 min debugging, not googleable, non-obvious fix, silent failure.
64	- Do **not** spawn `ROADMAP.md` / `IDEAS.md` / `LESSONS.md` / `TROUBLESHOOTING.md`. Three surfaces, always.
65	- A pitfall *graduates* to a Hard invariant below when it (a) recurs across machines, (b) silently corrupts state, or (c) has a non-obvious workaround. Link back to `pitfalls/<slug>.md`.
66	
67	## Chezmoi templating conventions
68	
69	**Hard rule**: before adding `{{ if eq .profile … }}`, ask if the predicate is auto-detectable. If yes, use `.chezmoi.os` / `.chezmoi.arch` / `.chezmoi.hostname`. `.profile` is for user-role choices only. Values are limited to `macos`, `ubuntu_desktop`, `ubuntu_server` — do **not** introduce new values for OS/arch facts (historical `macos_intel` profile was removed for exactly this reason).
70	
71	**Hard rule — prefer XDG paths.** When a tool supports both a `$HOME`-root dotfile and an XDG path (`~/.config/<tool>/…`), manage the XDG copy (`dot_config/<tool>/…`) to keep `$HOME` tidy; only use a root dotfile when the tool can't read XDG. For tools that error when *both* paths exist (e.g. AeroSpace), also remove the legacy root file via a gated `.chezmoiremove` entry. Full rule + lookup-order caveats: [docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md → A1](docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md).
72	
73	| Predicate | Use |
74	|---|---|
75	| Any macOS | `eq .chezmoi.os "darwin"` |
76	| Any Linux | `eq .chezmoi.os "linux"` |
77	| Apple Silicon | `eq .chezmoi.arch "arm64"` (in darwin scope) or `and (eq .chezmoi.os "darwin") (eq .chezmoi.arch "arm64")` |
78	| Intel Mac | `and (eq .chezmoi.os "darwin") (eq .chezmoi.arch "amd64")` |
79	| Desktop vs headless | `.profile` — `ubuntu_desktop` / `ubuntu_server` |
80	
81	Decision table, before/after examples, `macos_intel` migration: [docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md).
82	
83	## Hard repo invariants
84	
85	### Validate app configs with the app, not just syntax
86	
87	Template rendering / YAML / TOML / JSON syntax is not enough. If the app exposes a config check, parser, dry-run, or debug command, run it against the rendered config before declaring done (e.g. `codex debug …` for `~/.codex/config.toml`; `tmux source-file` / `display-menu` smoke for tmux; `mkdocs build --strict` for docs; for Ansible run the narrowest practical play/tag/check-mode or container smoke — `--syntax-check` alone is a first pass). If a validator cannot be run, say so explicitly in the final report and name the missing command/host/credential.
88	
89	### `primaryShell` choice gates `chsh` only — both shells always deploy
90	
91	`primaryShell` (`zsh` | `bash`, default `zsh`) **only** governs which login shell `chsh` switches to. Both `~/.zshrc`, `~/.bashrc`, `~/.config/{shell,zsh,bash}/` deploy everywhere — users routinely drop into the other shell ad-hoc.
92	
93	**Hard rules**:
94	
95	- Do **not** add `{{ if eq .primaryShell … }}` gates around `dot_zshrc.tmpl`, `dot_bashrc.tmpl`, or `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/**`.
96	- Do **not** gate the zsh / bash ansible roles' **package install** task on `primary_shell` — only `chsh` is gated. macOS bash 5.x brew install + `/etc/shells` whitelist are gated on `primary_shell == "bash"` (zsh-primary mac users skip the brew formula).
97	- Do **not** rely on `$SHELL` — it reflects `/etc/passwd`, lags `chsh` until next login. Use `$ZSH_VERSION` / `$BASH_VERSION`.
98	
99	ble.sh + oh-my-bash 12-step init order in `dot_bashrc.tmpl` is load-bearing: `ble.sh --attach=none` MUST source before bash-preexec/starship; `ble-attach` MUST be the last call before secrets/adhoc; OMB's `autosuggestions` / `syntax-highlighting` / `history-substring-search` plugins MUST be excluded (ble.sh provides natives; double-init causes flicker). Full breakdown: [docs/shells/bash.md](docs/shells/bash.md).
100	
101	### Three-tier user-local override layer
102	
103	User overrides live in **six** untracked files: shared POSIX (`~/.shellrc.adhoc`, `~/.shellrc.secrets`) and per-shell (`~/.zshrc.adhoc`, `~/.bashrc.adhoc`, `~/.config/zsh/secrets.zsh`, `~/.config/bash/secrets.sh`). All six in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`. Default target: shared. Drop to per-shell only when shell-specific syntax is required.
104	
105	**Load order** in both `dot_zshrc.tmpl` and `dot_bashrc.tmpl`:
106	
107	```
108	managed modules → shared secrets → per-shell secrets → shared adhoc → per-shell adhoc
109	```
110	
111	Secrets before adhoc (so adhoc can read secret vars); shared before per-shell (per-shell wins on conflict).
112	
113	**Hard rules**: never add the shared files to chezmoi management; never auto-stub the `*.secrets` files (empty secrets footgun); the shared adhoc stub heredoc lives in BOTH `dot_zshrc.tmpl` AND `dot_bashrc.tmpl` (first shell to run wins; second sees the file and skips) — keep both heredoc bodies in sync. Full matrix: [docs/shells/adhoc-and-secrets.md](docs/shells/adhoc-and-secrets.md).
114	
115	### `enableVimMode` gates shell + tmux vim, NOT Neovim or editors
116	
117	`enableVimMode` (bool, default `true`) gates **shell modal editing + tmux vim navigation only**. Neovim and every editor config (VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity/Codex/OpenCode/Cursor-CLI) are **never** affected. Full catalog of the 7 gated templated files + 2 first-seed files (`marimo.toml`, btop's `btop.conf`): [docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md](docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md).
118	
119	**Hard rules**:
120	
121	- Do **not** gate anything under `dot_config/nvim/` — Neovim is inherently vim by design.
122	- Do **not** gate editor configs (`.chezmoitemplates/editor/`, `dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl`, `dot_config/opencode/modify_*.json.tmpl`, `dot_cursor/modify_cli-config.json`) — the flag's semantic is shells + tmux only. Editors want vim → install the editor's vim extension.
123	- Do **not** broaden the gate to `bindkey -M viins`/`vicmd` calls inside `dot_config/zsh/tools/*.zsh` — harmless no-ops without zsh-vi-mode loaded.
124	- The `minimal` bundle in `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py` forces `enableVimMode = False` (CI/Docker). Don't change without explicit user request.
125	- New vim-touched file → follow the "Yes, gate it" / "No, leave it alone" flow in `docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md` → "For maintainers", and add it to the catalog table in that same page.
126	
127	### Install vs upgrade is split on purpose
128	
129	`chezmoi apply` + ansible is **install-only** (`state: present`, `creates:`). Explicit upgrade path: [`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`](scripts/upgrade_tools.sh) via `just upgrade-*`. `scripts/**` is in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`, so the upgrade script runs from the repo, never deployed.
130	
131	**Hard rules**:
132	
133	- Do **not** rewrite ansible roles to `state: latest`.
134	- Do **not** add `apt upgrade` / system package bumps to default scope.
135	- **Minimum-version exception**: a role MAY auto-upgrade a single tool inside `chezmoi apply` when it legitimately needs a newer version (e.g. `python_uv_tools` needs `uv >= 0.8.5` for `--with-executables-from`). MUST detect install style (brew vs curl/standalone) and dispatch — never blindly `uv self update` (no-op on brew uv) or `brew upgrade uv` (errors if not a brew formula). Dispatch helper is mirrored in `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh::cat_uv()` and `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/tasks/main.yml`. See [docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md](docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md), [pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md](pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md), [pitfalls/ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md](pitfalls/ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md).
136	- **`with_executables_from:` entries MUST also declare `extra_binaries:`** in `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml`. Without it the install guard short-circuits on hosts where the primary binary already exists, and entry-point shims are never written (silent missing `jupyter` / `jupyter-notebook` despite `jupyter-lab` present). Audit: `yq '.python_uv_tools[] | select(.with_executables_from) | select(.extra_binaries == null) | .name' …` MUST print nothing. See [pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md](pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md).
137	- New upgrade category: [docs/this_repo/upgrades.md → Adding a new category](docs/this_repo/upgrades.md). For a tool already managed by brew/uv/npm/cargo/dotnet/gem/mise: do nothing — generic `upgrade` picks it up.
138	
139	### Sudo session is shared across all run-scripts
140	
141	All three `run_*` scripts share one sudo session via `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` — user prompted once at `chezmoi apply` start, reused silently downstream.
142	
143	**Hard rules**:
144	
145	- Do **not** re-implement `sudo -k` / `sudo -v` / TTY-read logic. Call the shared helper.
146	- Do **not** run `sudo -k` (invalidates the cache for the whole flow).
147	- Do **not** register a `trap … EXIT` that removes state (next run-script needs it).
148	- Do **not** read the password into a shell variable. Always `sudo -S <file`.
149	- Do **not** replace `_sudo_spawn_watchdog`'s `setsid`/`nohup` fallback with bare `setsid` — macOS lacks `setsid(1)` in base, the backgrounded failure is silent (redirected to `/dev/null`), and every run-script then re-prompts because `_sudo_state_valid`'s `kill -0` probe finds a dead PID. See [`pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md`](pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md).
150	
151	**Adding a new sudo surface in a run-script**:
152	
153	1. `{{ include "scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh" }}` near the top of the template.
154	2. Set the `NEED_SUDO` template flag.
155	3. Call `sudo_session_init "yourlabel"`; branch on return code + `sudo_session_skip_reason`.
156	4. Privileged commands via `sudo_run …` or `-e @$CHEZMOI_ANSIBLE_BECOME_FILE` for ansible.
157	
158	**Non-interactive password injection** (used by `scripts/fleet/apply.py` over SSH): `sudo_session_init` adopts `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` (a 0600 file) instead of prompting on `/dev/tty`. **Never** read `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` directly — always go through `sudo_session_init`. Full API + state + cleanup model: [docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md](docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md).
159	
160	### fleet-apply counter-intuitive defaults
161	
162	Full docs: [`docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md). Load-bearing invariants:
163	
164	- **`drift` ≠ `failed`**. When chezmoi can't prompt to overwrite a hand-edited file (no PTY over SSH), the host shows yellow ⚠ `drift` with paths listed — but it does **not** count toward exit code. Don't auto-"fix" drift unless asked. Resolution: hand-fix the remote, or `--force` to let template win.
165	- **`fleet-apply-file PATH` skips `run_*` scripts** (uses `chezmoi apply --exclude=scripts`). Ansible / Brewfile changes will NOT execute — use full `fleet-apply` for ansible iterations.
166	- **`--branch BRANCH` is no-op on local hosts** (the local source dir IS the user's editor working tree). Local hosts log warn and run against working tree as-is. The flag also forces mode to `apply`.
167	- **Install-only by design** (inherits the previous invariant). `just upgrade-*` must run on each host; fleet-apply does NOT broadcast upgrades.
168	- **Process substitution + sentinel are load-bearing**: `> >(tee -a $log) 2>&1 & _cz_pid=$!; wait $_cz_pid; _rc=$?; echo $_rc > $sentinel`. `--status` / `--tail` / `--watch` + SIGHUP trap depend on `$_cz_pid` pointing to chezmoi, not tee. Don't change to a pipeline.
169	- **Conservative drift classifier**: `_classify_drift()` only downgrades stderr lines matching the exact `chezmoi: <path>: could not open a new TTY: open /dev/tty:` fingerprint. Anything unrecognised stays `failed`. Don't broaden without explicit user request — silent downgrades hide real errors.
170	- **`fleet-status` ≠ `fleet-apply-status`** — easy to confuse:
171	  - `just fleet-status` → **pre-flight readiness probe** (states: `up-to-date`, `behind`, `ahead`, `dirty`, `drift`, `ready-to-update`, `busy`, `init-in-progress`, `toml-mismatch`, `not-init`, `no-source`, `no-chezmoi`, `unreachable`). Run **before** `fleet-apply`. Always exits 0; use `--readiness-json | jq` for scripted gates. `fleet-status-quick` skips remote `git fetch`.
172	  - `just fleet-apply-status` → **process-liveness probe** of `~/.cache/fleet-apply/<host>.{pid,sentinel,log}`. Run **during/after**. Pairs with `fleet-apply-tail` / `fleet-apply-watch` / `fleet-apply-kill`.
173	  - `toml-mismatch` catches a remote's `chezmoi.toml` missing prompt keys that current `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` requires, via static `_PROMPT_KEY_RE` comparison — `chezmoi dump-config` cannot be used (would re-evaluate the very template we're inspecting).
174	  - `fleet-edit` + `fleet-status` are forgiving (auto-seed / exit 0 with hint); `fleet-apply` keeps strict exit-2 on missing inventory. Don't unify.
175	
176	### `modify_` and `create_` prefix semantics
177	
178	- **`modify_`** files are executable scripts: chezmoi pipes current target contents to stdin, expects new contents on stdout. Used for `~/.claude/settings.json` (jq overlay), editor `settings.json` (VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity), agent CLI configs (`~/.cursor/cli-config.json`, `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml`), and `~/.gitconfig` (preserves `[credential "<URL>"]` blocks injected by `gh auth setup-git` so the gh-managed absolute path to the local `gh` binary — different on Intel mac / Apple Silicon / Linuxbrew — survives `chezmoi apply`). **Never** `chezmoi add` a `modify_` target — it would overwrite the script with the live file.
179	- **`create_`** files seed once; chezmoi never touches contents after. Used for `~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json` and editor `keybindings.json`. Refresh baseline by copying directly: `cp <target> "$(chezmoi source-path <target>)"`. `chezmoi add` strips the prefix; `chezmoi re-add` silently skips.
180	
181	Case studies + presence-gating in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`: [docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md). Three agent CLI overlays (incl. the Claude hook-aware merger that coexists with [CodeIsland](https://github.com/wxtsky/CodeIsland)'s auto-installed hook entries without ping-ponging): [docs/tools/agent-overlays.md](docs/tools/agent-overlays.md).
182	
183	### Tmux popup menu: ≥ 3.3 required + must fit terminal height
184	
185	The popup menu (bound to `prefix + Space` and `prefix + e`) is **generated** by `~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`, not inline in `keybindings.conf`. Two unrelated tmux quirks force this:
186	
187	1. **Position clamping (tmux ≥ 3.3)**: `display-menu -x R -y P` is silently suppressed on tmux 3.2a (Ubuntu 22.04 apt) when it would place the menu past the terminal edge. tmux 3.3+ clamps. `devtools` role auto-upgrades on Debian/Ubuntu (Linuxbrew first, else [`nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage`](https://github.com/nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage) extracted to `~/.local/share/tmux-appimage/` with a `~/.local/bin/tmux` shim). Run `tmux kill-server` once after — running servers keep the old binary in memory.
188	2. **Menu-too-tall silent failure (all versions)**: `display-menu` does **not** paginate. Taller than terminal → entire popup suppressed, no error, nothing in `tmux show-messages`. `man tmux`: _"If the menu is too large to fit on the terminal, it is not displayed."_ Misdiagnosed for hours as a CSI-u keysym bug after a 50-row flat menu started failing on smaller heights.
189	
190	**Hard rules**:
191	
192	- **Top menu cap ≈ 14 rows**. Generator reads `#{client_height}` and tier-trims; retest at heights 14 / 22 / 60 when changing tiers. Push lower-frequency items into category submenus.
193	- **Submenus = separate scripts**, each `exec tmux display-menu …`. Quoting context resets per script.
194	- **Complex commands** (anything with `{`, `}`, `;`, backticks, nested fzf binds) MUST live in their own script. tmux's parser treats `{}` / `;` as command-block delimiters even inside `'…'` inside `"…"`, silently aborting parse.
195	- **Test by shrinking the terminal vertically**. Full-height verification does not catch the height-fit failure.
196	
197	See `pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md` (red herrings included) and `pitfalls/yazi-tmux-popup-crash.md`.
198	
199	### Key tmux settings for coding agents
200	
201	Non-obvious settings other tools depend on; do not remove without checking:
202	
203	- `extended-keys on` + `terminal-features 'xterm*:extkeys'` — forwards Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+/, Ctrl+digit to inner apps (Claude Code, Neovim, …). **Never use `always`** — re-encodes EVERY `Ctrl+letter` as CSI-u including the LF (Ctrl+J) embedded in pasted multi-line text → ble.sh inserts `^[[106;5u` literally instead of newline. See `pitfalls/tmux-extended-keys-always-paste.md`.
204	- `escape-time 0` — eliminates ESC delay for Neovim.
205	- `set-clipboard on` + `terminal-features …:clipboard` (for `xterm*`, `ghostty*`, `alacritty*`) — OSC 52 over SSH without terminfo `Ms`. Paired with SSH-conditional `vim.g.clipboard = vim.ui.clipboard.osc52` in `dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`. See [docs/tools/tmux/README.md → OSC 52 Clipboard](docs/tools/tmux/README.md).
206	- `allow-passthrough on` — OSC passthrough for terminal images.
207	- macOS terminals must send Option as Meta/Esc+ for `M-` keybindings (theme switching, layouts, fine resize). Ghostty/cmux: `macos-option-as-alt = left` in `dot_config/ghostty/config`. See [docs/tools/ghostty.md](docs/tools/ghostty.md).
208	
209	Full tmux config breakdown / theme switching / keybindings / troubleshooting: [docs/tools/tmux/](docs/tools/tmux/).
210	
211	### Zellij `default_mode "locked"`
212	
213	`dot_config/zellij/config.kdl` uses `default_mode "locked"` so all keys pass through to inner apps by default. `Ctrl+G` to unlock Zellij commands. First Zellij launch (no existing config): select the "Unlock-First (non-colliding)" keybinding preset.

## 1. `dot_config/shell/99_chezmoi_reload.sh` (full analysis)

Absolute path: `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/99_chezmoi_reload.sh` (124 lines)

**What it does:** Post-`chezmoi apply` reload *hint* system plus the `cas`/`cau`/`czcfg` wrappers. It is the single source of truth for both the hint backend and the shell-hook registration.

**Sentinel file:** `_CZ_RELOAD_SENTINEL="${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/chezmoi/last-apply"` (line 26). Each shell also records a per-session birth marker via `mktemp` (line 27). The check (lines 47-69) fires at most once per session, only when the sentinel is newer than the session birth marker (`-nt` comparison, line 51), guarded by `_CZ_RELOAD_SHOWN`.

**Opt-out:** `export CHEZMOI_RELOAD_HINT=0` short-circuits at line 24.

**Existing shell-detection helper** `_chezmoi_reload_current_shell()` (lines 36-44) — this is the reusable helper you'll want:
```sh
_chezmoi_reload_current_shell() {
    if [[ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]]; then
        printf 'zsh'
    elif [[ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ]]; then
        printf 'bash'
    else
        printf '%s' "$(basename "${SHELL:-sh}")"
    fi
}
```
Note it resolves the *current interpreter* via `$ZSH_VERSION`/`$BASH_VERSION` rather than `$SHELL`, deliberately (comment lines 34-35).

**Functions/aliases defined:**
- `_chezmoi_reload_cleanup()` (lines 29-31) — trap on EXIT to remove birth marker.
- `_chezmoi_reload_current_shell()` (lines 36-44).
- `_chezmoi_reload_check()` (lines 47-69) — the once-per-session hint.
- `cas()` (lines 74-79) — `chezmoi apply "$@"` then `exec "$sh" -l`.
- `cau()` (lines 80-85) — `chezmoi update "$@"` then `exec "$sh" -l`.
- `czcfg()` (lines 94-105) — reconfigure prompts via `uv run` on `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py`.
- No `cas`/`cau`/`czcfg` are aliases; all are functions.

**Does it already re-source the rc file?** No. The only in-place reload path is via `cas`/`cau`, which do `exec "$sh" -l` (a full login-shell replacement, lines 78 & 84) — NOT a `source ~/.zshrc`. There is no existing function that re-sources the rc file in the current process.

**The hint message** it prints (lines 63-64 colored, 66-67 plain) tells the user to run one of two things. With `sh` = current shell and `rc="~/.${sh}rc"` (lines 55-56):

Neither template runs live `$ZSH_VERSION`/`$BASH_VERSION` detection for reload purposes — each template *is* the entry point for exactly one shell, and detection is done by the shared helper in `99_chezmoi_reload.sh` (section 1). Relevant facts:

64	# Run CMD for at most DURATION, then send SIGINT (same as Ctrl-C) so a script's

70	#   DURATION takes GNU timeout suffixes: 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d, or bare seconds.
71	#   RUN_FOR_SIGNAL      signal sent on expiry (default INT)
72	#   RUN_FOR_KILL_AFTER  grace before SIGKILL (default 5s)
73	# Exit status: 124 = the time-box was hit (command still running); otherwise
74	#   the command's own exit status passes through.

77	#   run-for 30s ./some-infinite-loop.sh

81			return 2

86			return 127

359	# --- claude-plans-here -----------------------------------------------------
360	# Scaffold or update project-local .claude/settings.json so Claude Code's
361	# /plan files land in ./.claude/plans/ (kept inside the repo) instead of the
362	# user-global plansDirectory. Pairs well with the agent-history-hygiene skill,
363	# which can then redact + commit the plan files alongside the diff.
364	#
365	# Also offers to import "orphan" plans — plans previously written under the
366	# global ~/.claude/plans/ that belong to this project. Detection: scan
367	# ~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/*.jsonl (where Claude Code logs sessions
368	# per cwd; encoding maps '/' and '.' to '-') for authoritative write records:
369	# Write/Edit/MultiEdit tool_use file paths, newer toolUseResult.filePath
370	# records, and ExitPlanMode planFilePath fields. This avoids false positives
371	# from sessions that merely *mentioned* a plan path in conversation.
372	#
373	# Usage: claude-plans-here [-f] [-y]
374	#   -f   auto-yes the settings.json merge prompt
375	#   -y   auto-yes the orphan-plan copy prompt
376	claude-plans-here() {
377		force_settings=0
378		force_orphans=0
379		while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
380			case "$1" in
381			-f) force_settings=1 ;;
382			-y) force_orphans=1 ;;
383			-h | --help)
384				echo "Usage: claude-plans-here [-f] [-y]"
385				echo "  -f   auto-yes the settings.json merge prompt"
386				echo "  -y   auto-yes the orphan-plan copy prompt"
387				return 0
388				;;
389			*)
390				echo "claude-plans-here: unknown flag '$1'" >&2
391				return 1
392				;;
393			esac
394			shift
395		done
396	
397		target=".claude/settings.json"
398		mkdir -p .claude/plans
399	
400		if [ ! -e "$target" ]; then
401			cat >"$target" <<'EOF'
402	{
403	  "plansDirectory": "./.claude/plans"
404	}
405	EOF
406			echo "Wrote $PWD/$target"
407		else
408			if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
409				echo "claude-plans-here: jq required to merge into existing $target" >&2
410				return 1
411			fi
412	
413			ans=y
414			if [ "$force_settings" = "0" ]; then
415				printf '%s exists. Merge plansDirectory into it? [y/N] ' "$target"
416				read -r ans
417			fi

419			case "$ans" in

421				tmp="$(mktemp)" || return 1
422				if jq --arg p "./.claude/plans" '. + {plansDirectory: $p}' "$target" >"$tmp"; then
423					mv "$tmp" "$target"
424					echo "Merged plansDirectory into $PWD/$target"
425				else
426					rm -f "$tmp"
427					echo "claude-plans-here: jq failed; $target unchanged" >&2
428					return 1
429				fi
430				;;
431			esac
432		fi
433	
434		_claude_plans_here_import_orphans "$force_orphans"
435		unset force_settings force_orphans target ans tmp
436	}

438	# Internal: scan ~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd|encoded-git-root>/*.jsonl
439	# for authoritative records that wrote into ~/.claude/plans/, list the ones
440	# still living in the global dir and not yet copied locally, prompt y/N.
441	_claude_plans_here_import_orphans() {
442		force="$1"
443		global_plans="$HOME/.claude/plans"
444		[ -d "$global_plans" ] || return 0
445	
446		# Claude Code projects/ encoding: replace each '/' and '.' with '-'.
447		enc_cwd="$(printf '%s' "$PWD" | tr '/.' '--')"
448		enc_root=""
449		if command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1; then
450			groot="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)"
451			if [ -n "$groot" ] && [ "$groot" != "$PWD" ]; then
452				enc_root="$(printf '%s' "$groot" | tr '/.' '--')"
453			fi
454		fi
455	
456		proj_dirs=""
457		[ -d "$HOME/.claude/projects/$enc_cwd" ] && proj_dirs="$HOME/.claude/projects/$enc_cwd"
458		[ -n "$enc_root" ] && [ -d "$HOME/.claude/projects/$enc_root" ] &&
459			proj_dirs="${proj_dirs}
460	$HOME/.claude/projects/$enc_root"
461		[ -z "$proj_dirs" ] && return 0
462	
463		jsonl_files="$(
464			printf '%s\n' "$proj_dirs" | while IFS= read -r d; do
465				[ -n "$d" ] || continue
466				find "$d" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.jsonl' 2>/dev/null
467			done
468		)"
469		[ -z "$jsonl_files" ] && return 0
470	
471		matches="$(_claude_plans_here_find_plan_paths "$global_plans" "$jsonl_files")"
472		[ -z "$matches" ] && return 0
473	
474		candidates=""
475		count=0
476		while IFS= read -r m; do
477			[ -f "$m" ] || continue
478			base="${m##*/}"
479			[ -e ".claude/plans/$base" ] && continue
480			candidates="$candidates
481	$m"
482			count=$((count + 1))
483		done <<EOF
484	$matches
485	EOF
486		[ "$count" = 0 ] && return 0
487	
488		echo
489		echo "Found $count orphan plan(s) in ~/.claude/plans/ linked to this project:"
490		printf '%s\n' "$candidates" | while IFS= read -r m; do
491			[ -z "$m" ] && continue
492			printf '  - %s\n' "${m#$HOME/}"
493		done
494	
495		ans=y
496		if [ "$force" = "0" ]; then
497			printf 'Copy them into ./.claude/plans/ (originals kept)? [y/N] '
498			read -r ans
499		fi
500		case "$ans" in
501		y | Y | yes | YES | Yes) ;;
502		*) return 0 ;;
503		esac
504	
505		copied=0
506		while IFS= read -r m; do
507			[ -z "$m" ] && continue
508			cp -n "$m" .claude/plans/ 2>/dev/null && copied=$((copied + 1))
509		done <<EOF
510	$candidates
511	EOF
512		echo "Copied plan(s) into $PWD/.claude/plans/"
513		unset force global_plans enc_cwd enc_root groot proj_dirs jsonl_files matches candidates count m base ans copied
514	}
515	
516	_claude_plans_here_find_plan_paths() {
517		global_plans="$1"
518		jsonl_files="$2"
519	
520		if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
521			printf '%s\n' "$jsonl_files" | while IFS= read -r f; do
522				[ -r "$f" ] || continue
523				jq -r --arg gp "$global_plans" '
524					def planpath:
525						select(type == "string")
526						| select(startswith($gp + "/") and test("\\.md$"));
527					[
528						(.message.content[]?
529							| select(.type == "tool_use")
530							| select(.name == "Write" or .name == "Edit" or .name == "MultiEdit")
531							| (.input.file_path?, .input.filePath?, .input.path?)),
532						(.message.content[]?
533							| select(.type == "tool_use" and .name == "ExitPlanMode")
534							| (.input.planFilePath?, .input.plan_file_path?)),
535						(.toolUseResult.filePath?, .toolUseResult.file_path?, .toolUseResult.path?),
536						(.toolUseResult.planFilePath?, .toolUseResult.plan_file_path?),
537						(.planFilePath?, .plan_file_path?)
538					]
539					| .[]?
540					| planpath
541				' "$f" 2>/dev/null
542			done | sort -u
543		else
544			# Cold-start fallback for hosts without jq. Less precise than the JSON
545			# parser, but still scoped to lines that contain write/result markers.
546			re_prefix="$(printf '%s' "$global_plans" | sed 's/[.[\*^$()+?{|]/\\&/g')"
547			printf '%s\n' "$jsonl_files" | while IFS= read -r f; do
548				[ -r "$f" ] || continue
549				grep -hE '"name"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"(Write|Edit|MultiEdit)"|"toolUseResult"|"planFilePath"' "$f" 2>/dev/null
550			done |
551				grep -oE "${re_prefix}/[A-Za-z0-9_.+-]+\.md" |
552				sort -u
553		fi
554	
555		unset global_plans jsonl_files f re_prefix
556	}

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="Read"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Read**</summary>
 `./pitfalls/zsh-parse-error-on-resource-after-bw-completion-aliased-name.md`

```text
1	# `parse error near \`()'` when re-sourcing `~/.zshrc` after a tool's completion script registered an alias matching one of our function names
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section):
4	
5	- Re-sourcing `~/.zshrc` (NOT first source — works fine on shell startup)
6	  fails with:
7	  ```
8	  ❯ source ~/.zshrc
9	  /home/<user>/.config/shell/10_aliases.sh:66: defining function based on alias `bw-update-completion'
10	  /home/<user>/.config/shell/10_aliases.sh:66: parse error near `()'
11	  ```
12	- Line number points at a perfectly normal POSIX function definition
13	  (`name() { ... }`) that has been in the repo unchanged for months and
14	  still works in fresh shells.
15	- A fresh `zsh -l` / new terminal tab is fine. Only `source ~/.zshrc`
16	  inside an already-running interactive shell triggers it.
17	- `bash` does not reproduce — bash silently allows function-and-alias
18	  with the same name.
19	- Removing the function definition makes the error vanish (red herring —
20	  the function is fine).
21	
22	## Root cause
23	
24	zsh option `ALIAS_FUNC_DEF` is **off by default** since 5.8. With it off,
25	zsh refuses to parse `name() { ... }` (POSIX function syntax) if `name`
26	is currently registered as an alias — and it errors with the `parse
27	error near \`()'` cited above. The `function name { ... }` ksh-style
28	syntax is **immune** because `function` is a reserved word that
29	suppresses alias expansion of the immediately following name.
30	
31	The latent collision in this repo:
32	
33	1. `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh` defines a function
34	   `bw-update-completion` to refresh the cached `bw` (Bitwarden CLI)
35	   shell completion file.
36	2. `dot_config/zsh/tools/95_bitwarden.zsh` later sources
37	   `~/.cache/zsh/bw_completion.zsh` if present.
38	3. Newer `bw` versions (post April 2025-ish) emit an
39	   `alias bw-update-completion=...` line inside that completion script
40	   — older versions did not.
41	4. After `bw completion --shell zsh` is regenerated against a newer bw
42	   binary, sourcing the cache file installs the alias **after** the
43	   function was already defined.
44	5. **First** `~/.zshrc` source: function defined first, alias added
45	   later — both coexist, alias wins at command lookup but no parse
46	   error happens (the function definition was already parsed).
47	6. **Second** `source ~/.zshrc` in the same interactive shell:
48	   `10_aliases.sh` is re-parsed; this time the alias already exists at
49	   parse time → `defining function based on alias` → `parse error`.
50	
51	The same trap applies to **any** function in `dot_config/shell/*.sh`
52	whose name a tool's completion script (or plugin) might later create as
53	an alias. The function name does not have to match `bw-*` or
54	`*-completion` — generic names are vulnerable too.
55	
56	## Fix
57	
58	Use the `function` keyword for any function whose name is even
59	plausibly aliasable by a tool's completion script:
60	
61	```sh
62	# ❌ Vulnerable — POSIX form, alias-checked at parse time in zsh
63	bw-update-completion() {
64	  ...
65	}
66	
67	# ✅ Safe — `function` keyword bypasses alias expansion of the name
68	function bw-update-completion {
69	  ...
70	}
71	```
72	
73	Both forms work in bash and zsh. The `function name { … }` form (no
74	`()`) is preferred over `function name() { … }` — the latter still
75	involves a `()` token that older POSIX-strict linters dislike, though
76	zsh/bash both accept it.
77	
78	This repo's actual fix: `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh:66` —
79	`bw-update-completion()` → `function bw-update-completion`.
80	
81	## Workaround in current shell
82	
83	If you hit the error and don't want to restart the shell:
84	
85	```sh
86	unalias bw-update-completion 2>/dev/null
87	source ~/.zshrc
88	```
89	
90	Until you re-source `~/.cache/zsh/bw_completion.zsh` again the alias
91	won't come back.
92	
93	## Defensive options NOT taken
94	
95	- **`unalias` defensively at the top of `10_aliases.sh`** — would have
96	  to enumerate every name. Doesn't generalize.
97	- **`unalias bw-update-completion`** in `95_bitwarden.zsh` after
98	  sourcing the completion cache — narrowly correct but won't help
99	  future tools that pull the same trick. Also makes the alias the
100	  completion script provides effectively unreachable.
101	- **`setopt ALIAS_FUNC_DEF`** globally — masks real bugs (the OPPOSITE
102	  case where you intend `name()` to redefine an aliased command).
103	  Don't.
104	
105	## Detecting recurrence
106	
107	If you write a new helper in `dot_config/shell/*.sh` and want to
108	verify nothing's already aliasing the name in your live shells:
109	
110	```sh
111	zsh -ic 'alias' | grep -F "<name>="
112	bash -ic 'alias' | grep -F "<name>="
113	```
114	
115	Returning nothing in both means you can use either function-definition
116	syntax safely. Returning anything → use `function name { … }`.
117	
118	## Why `bash` doesn't see it
119	
120	bash silently allows `name() { ... }` to coexist with `alias name=...`;
121	the function is callable via `\name` (backslash bypasses alias
122	expansion) or by `unalias` first. bash also has no equivalent of
123	`ALIAS_FUNC_DEF`. So a bash-only repo would never have noticed this
124	class of bug — a portable shell file shared between bash and zsh is
125	exactly where it bites.
126	
127	## Related
128	
129	- `dot_config/zsh/tools/95_bitwarden.zsh` — the `bw` completion cache
130	  loader.
131	- `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh` — the shared shell helpers,
132	  `bw-update-completion` lives here.
133	- AGENTS.md → "Custom aliases & shell functions → `docs/shells/aliases.md`"
134	  — three-tier file placement rule (shared `dot_config/shell/`, zsh-only
135	  `dot_config/zsh/`, bash-only `dot_config/bash/`).
136
```

# Plan: `source-rc` / `reload` — re-source the current shell's rc in place

## Context

After `chezmoi apply` (or `cau`), long-lived shell sessions don't see new aliases/
functions until they re-source their rc. Today that means the user manually types
`source ~/.zshrc` or `source ~/.bashrc` — having to remember which entry-point file
their current shell uses, knowledge others may not have. The post-apply reload *hint*
in `dot_config/shell/99_chezmoi_reload.sh` already prints this suggestion, but there
is no single command that just does it.

Goal: a tiny, self-documenting, cross-shell command `source-rc` that auto-detects the
running interpreter and re-sources the correct rc **in place** (keeps cwd, history,
session state) — the lightweight counterpart to the existing `exec`-based `cas`/`cau`.
Also unify the short `reload` alias, which today exists **only in bash**
(`dot_config/bash/10_aliases.bash:12`, `alias reload='. ~/.bashrc'`) with no zsh
equivalent — make it cross-shell as a short alias for `source-rc`.

Decision (confirmed with user): **`source-rc` + unify `reload`**; semantics = in-place
`source` (not `exec`).

## Design notes / constraints

- **Shared tier**: lives in `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh` (sourced by both shells
  via `load_modular_dir`), next to sibling utilities `run-for` / `bindings` /
  `ghostty-ssh-terminfo`. No new numbered file (matches repo convention). No completion
  files needed (plain function/alias, not an `executable_*` CLI).
- **`function` keyword is mandatory, not `name()`**: `source-rc`'s job is to re-source,
  which re-parses `10_aliases.sh` on every call. The `function source-rc { … }` form is
  immune to the `ALIAS_FUNC_DEF` re-source `parse error near \`()'` documented in
  `pitfalls/zsh-parse-error-on-resource-after-bw-completion-aliased-name.md` (same reason
  the `*-update-completion` helpers in this file already use it). `function` keyword is
  fine here because only zsh/bash ever source this file (never dash).
- **Inline the shell dispatch — do NOT reuse `_chezmoi_reload_current_shell`**: that
  helper lives in `99_chezmoi_reload.sh`, which (a) loads *after* `10_aliases.sh` and
  (b) early-returns entirely when `CHEZMOI_RELOAD_HINT=0`, so depending on it would make
  `source-rc` break under that opt-out. The dispatch is 3 lines; inline it.
- **Detect via `$ZSH_VERSION`/`$BASH_VERSION`, never `$SHELL`** (repo convention — `$SHELL`
  lags `chsh` until next login).
- **Parity with manual `source ~/.zshrc`**: re-sourcing re-runs starship/mise/atuin/motd
  etc. and inherits the same zsh re-source caveats. This is identical to what the user
  does by hand today; `exec zsh -l` / `cas` remain the heavier "guaranteed-clean" path.
- **Indentation is TAB** in `10_aliases.sh` — match it exactly.

## Changes

### 1. `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh` (add function + alias)

Add a new section (near the `run-for` / `bindings` utility cluster, e.g. after the
`run-for` block ~line 91). Use TAB indentation:

\```sh
# --- Reload shell config (source-rc / reload) ------------------------------
# Re-source the CURRENT shell's rc entry point in place, so a running session
# picks up new aliases/functions after `chezmoi apply` — without exec'ing a
# fresh login shell (that heavier path is `cas`/`cau` in 99_chezmoi_reload.sh).
# Dispatches on the live interpreter ($ZSH_VERSION/$BASH_VERSION), not $SHELL.
# `function` keyword (not `name()`) is deliberate: this re-parses 10_aliases.sh
# on every call, so it must be immune to the ALIAS_FUNC_DEF re-source parse
# error — see pitfalls/zsh-parse-error-on-resource-after-bw-completion-aliased-name.md.
function source-rc {
	if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
		_rc="$HOME/.zshrc"
	elif [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
		_rc="$HOME/.bashrc"
	else
		printf 'source-rc: unsupported shell (need zsh or bash)\n' >&2
		return 1
	fi
	if [ ! -f "$_rc" ]; then
		printf 'source-rc: %s not found (run chezmoi apply first?)\n' "$_rc" >&2
		unset _rc
		return 1
	fi
	printf 'source-rc: reloading %s\n' "$_rc"
	# shellcheck source=/dev/null
	. "$_rc"
	unset _rc
}
alias reload='source-rc'
\```

Notes: re-sourcing only *redefines* `source-rc` (no recursion — it's never re-called).
`reload` as an alias is re-source-safe (no function-name collision).

### 2. `dot_config/bash/10_aliases.bash` (remove now-shared bash-only `reload`)

Replace lines 11–12 (`# Re-source bashrc… / alias reload='. ~/.bashrc'`) with a pointer
comment. The shared `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh` loads *after* this file for bash
(`load_modular_dir "$BASH_CONFIG_DIR" bash` at `dot_bashrc.tmpl:94` runs before the shared
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/shell` layer at :114), so the shared `alias reload='source-rc'` wins —
removing the bash-only line just avoids a confusing double definition:

\```sh
# `reload` (re-source the current shell's rc) is now cross-shell — defined once
# in dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh as `alias reload='source-rc'`, which loads
# after this file for bash, so the shared definition wins. See `source-rc` there.
\```

### 3. `docs/shells/aliases.md` (mandatory mirror — CLAUDE.md rule)

Add two rows to the **Shell Utilities** section (`## Shell Utilities`, ~line 717), same
4-col table (`Command | Type | Source File | Description`):

\```
| `source-rc` | function | `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh` | Re-source the current shell's rc (`~/.zshrc` or `~/.bashrc`, auto-detected via `$ZSH_VERSION`/`$BASH_VERSION`) in place — pick up new aliases/functions after `chezmoi apply` without a fresh login shell (lighter than `cas`/`cau`). |
| `reload` | alias | `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh` | Short alias for `source-rc`. Now cross-shell (was bash-only `. ~/.bashrc`). |
\```

Also `grep -n 'reload' docs/shells/aliases.md`: if an existing bash-only `reload` row
exists elsewhere, update/relocate it to point at the new shared source (avoid a stale
`. ~/.bashrc` entry).

### 4. `docs/shells/aliases.zh-TW.md` (translated mirror)

Add the equivalent two rows to the matching Shell Utilities section, translated to match
the file's existing style. Same `grep` check for a stale `reload` row.

### (Optional, offer at implementation) `dot_config/shell/99_chezmoi_reload.sh`

Directly serves the user's discoverability motivation: update the post-apply hint
(lines 63–67) to name `source-rc` as the lightweight option, e.g.
`… run source-rc (or exec <sh> -l) to reload`. Small, but touches a load-bearing file —
will confirm before doing it; not part of the core change.

## Verification

1. **Syntax** (file is non-templated, source == target):
   - `zsh -n dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh`
   - `bash -n dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh`

```bash
set -e
repo="$PWD"
work="$(mktemp -d)"

# --- zsh test ---
zhome="$work/zh"; mkdir -p "$zhome"
cat > "$zhome/.zshrc" <<RC
source "$repo/dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh"
alias _srtest='echo hi'
RC

echo "===== ZSH ====="
HOME="$zhome" zsh -fc '
  source "'"$repo"'/dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh"
  # pitfall immunity: pre-existing alias of same name must NOT break the file re-parse
  alias source-rc="echo SHOULD_NOT_RUN"
  source "'"$repo"'/dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh" && echo "FUNC-KEYWORD-OK (function keyword survived alias collision)"
  unalias source-rc 2>/dev/null
  source-rc
  alias _srtest >/dev/null && echo "PICKUP-OK (_srtest defined after reload)" || echo "PICKUP-FAIL"
  print -r -- "reload -> $(alias reload)"
  source-rc >/dev/null && echo "DOUBLE-OK (second source-rc, no parse error)"
'

# --- bash test ---
bhome="$work/bh"; mkdir -p "$bhome"
cat > "$bhome/.bashrc" <<RC
source "$repo/dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh"
alias _srtest='echo hi'
RC

echo "===== BASH ====="
HOME="$bhome" bash --norc -c '
  shopt -s expand_aliases
  source "'"$repo"'/dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh"
  source-rc
  alias _srtest >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "PICKUP-OK (_srtest defined after reload)" || echo "PICKUP-FAIL"
  type reload
  source-rc >/dev/null && echo "DOUBLE-OK (second source-rc)"
'

# --- edge branches ---
echo "===== EDGE ====="
HOME="$work/missing" zsh -fc 'source "'"$repo"'/dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh"; source-rc; echo "exit=$?"' 2>&1 || true

rm -rf "$work"

## What changed

**`source-rc`** — a cross-shell function that auto-detects the running interpreter (`$ZSH_VERSION`/`$BASH_VERSION`, not `$SHELL`) and re-sources the right rc **in place** (`~/.zshrc` for zsh, `~/.bashrc` for bash), so a long-lived session picks up new aliases/functions after `chezmoi apply` without exec'ing a fresh shell. **`reload`** is now a short cross-shell alias for it (it was bash-only before).

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh` | Added `function source-rc { … }` (inline shell dispatch) + `alias reload='source-rc'`, next to `run-for`/`bindings` |
| `dot_config/bash/10_aliases.bash` | Removed the old bash-only `alias reload='. ~/.bashrc'`, left a pointer comment (shared def loads after this file for bash, so it wins) |
| `docs/shells/aliases.md` | Two rows under Shell Utilities |
| `docs/shells/aliases.zh-TW.md` | Same two rows, translated |

**Key guard**: `source-rc` uses the `function name { … }` keyword form on purpose — since its job is re-sourcing (which re-parses `10_aliases.sh` every call), it must be immune to the `ALIAS_FUNC_DEF` `parse error near \`()'` documented in `pitfalls/zsh-parse-error-...md`. _**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-03 06:34:17Z)**_

Fixed and committed. Here's what happened and what I did.

## What broke
My earlier `uv run mkdocs build --strict` wrote a 45 MB `site/` build directory into the repo root — which is also the chezmoi **source** root. `.gitignore` covered it (`/site/`), but `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` didn't, so `chezmoi apply` tried to deploy every generated file to `~/site/**` and died on a social-card PNG the aborted strict build never wrote.

## Fixes (2 commits)
- **`3c5d24a`** — added `site` + `site/**` to `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` (in the "Repo tooling that must not deploy to $HOME" block, next to `mkdocs.yml`). Verified: with a dummy `site/index.html` present, `chezmoi managed` now excludes it, and the template still renders. This is a real latent gap — `CLAUDE.md` tells contributors to run `mkdocs build --strict` on doc changes, so anyone doing that locally would have hit the same wall.
- Removed the stray `site/` directory (git-ignored build artifact, regenerable).

Your earlier feature commit `0ea8fad` (source-rc / reload) is intact.

## You can retry now
`cas` will work — chezmoi no longer sees `site/`. Note `cas` will `exec` a fresh login shell after applying, so it also picks up the new `source-rc`/`reload` immediately.

One caveat for future doc work: `mkdocs build` aborts under `--strict` because of **pre-existing** anchor-drift + `mkdocs_llmstxt` warnings (tracked in `backlog/mkdocs-anchor-drift.md`) — unrelated to your configs. If you want to build docs locally without the artifact lingering, `uv run mkdocs build -d /tmp/site` keeps the output out of the repo root entirely.
